The exact finite probe tested 1,814,428 three-charge middle gaps through a=44
without failure. It also tested symmetrized midpoint comparisons at distances

statements. The largest observed distance-two endpoint sum divided by the

bound by one middle square is already false in this scan.

## Choice of representation

The previous worker proved that each cut term is coefficient-log-concave,
but found negative pairwise mixed gaps even on actual source words. I tested
aggregation by cut position and by the individual term's polynomial degree.
Chronological accumulation fails. Degree aggregation remains a candidate,
not a theorem. All experiments retain the raw integer coefficients and zeros.

For a source a/b, write w=central28(path) followed by B. Let M_s(w) be its
exact s-cut masks, and p_m(y)=maskWeight340(y,y,1,m). Define

    G_w(s,d;y) = sum_{m in M_s(w), degree(p_m)=d} p_m(y).

No multiplicity is discarded. The inherited coefficient bridge reads

    A(i,j) = [y^j] sum_d G_w(s,d;y),  i+j=a+s.

The new degree computation does not expand p_m. Keep a gap-degree state D,
initially 1. Skipping A resets D to 0; skipping B increments D. Selecting
a letter r adds D+1_{r=B} to the total term degree and resets D to 1. The
unselected suffix contributes zero to the total degree. mask_natDegree07a7
proves this exact equality for every mask over real polynomials, using
constant coefficient one to exclude zero factors. The integer source
coefficient bridge remains exact. There is no coefficient normalization.
The generic commutative-ring identities use this structural degree statistic;
they do not assert that it equals polynomial degree in positive characteristic.
The checked real-ring interpretation and inherited coefficientwise integer-to-real
map identify the intended characteristic-zero weights.

The bound degree(m)<=1+2*length(m) proves finite exhaustion for every word,
without a denominator bound. Thus a degree prefix beyond that bound equals
the whole cut polynomial. This is a representation theorem, not an inequality.

## Positive three-state recurrence

Introduce x for cut count, z for individual term degree, and retain y as the
original coefficient variable. The marked polynomial is

    H_w(x,y,z) = sum_m x^(number of cuts) z^(degree(p_m)) p_m(y).

For each partial mask let W be its accumulated marked weight, let
H=W*z^D*(p+1), and Z=W*z^D, where p is the current skipped-gap charge.
Start from (W,H,Z)=(1,z(1+y),z). If C denotes the selected contribution,
the forward updates are

    A: C=x H;
       (W,H,Z) -> (W+C, W+z(1+y)C, W+z C).

    B: C=x z(1+y)H;
       (W,H,Z) -> (W+C, zy H+z(1+y)Z+z(1+y)C, z Z+z C).

The final W is H_w. Every matrix entry has nonnegative coefficients.
MarkovDegreeTransfer07a7 proves the equivalent backward three-state scalar
identity over every commutative ring. It also proves the marked-mask sum
and the z=1 specialization. MarkovDegreeBridge07a7 connects ordinary x
coefficient extraction to exactly s cuts and ordinary z coefficient
extraction to the structural degree layers. At z=1 the inherited source
identity gives the literal raw integer numerator coefficients.

The polynomial coefficient/nonnegative-interval support result for each
layer follows from the inherited corresponding properties of every mask.
This prevents an internal-zero-gap ambiguity in a future adjacent-to-PF2
argument, but supplies no adjacent inequality itself. Positivity of the
three-state transfer is not a proof of coefficient log-concavity.

## Two source-specific obstructions

At source 11/13, path RRRRRL, the extended word is B^5 A B^6. The first
eight single-cut positions sum to

    8+20y+20y^2+14y^3+10y^4+6y^5+2y^6.

Its j=2,3,4 triple is [20,14,10] and has gap -4. The full one-cut sum is

    12+32y+36y^2+28y^3+20y^4+12y^5+4y^6.

The corresponding original points (10,2),(9,3),(8,4) lie in the pinned
polygon and have [36,28,20], gap 64. The append identity for one-cut sums
is proved universally, so the partial sum has an exact chronological meaning.
This invalidates induction through arbitrary chronological partial sums;
it is not a counterexample to the published conjecture.

At source 2/7, path LLR, w=AAB AAB, the two-cut degree layers are

    G(2,0)=1, G(2,1)=3+3y, G(2,2)=11+25y+14y^2.

The constant coefficients [1,3,11] fail log-concavity in d. Thus the refined
array is not jointly discrete-midpoint-log-concave in (d,j), even on a source.
The d direction is auxiliary, not one of the three pinned directions.
The complete source diagonal has [15,28,14] at (4,0),(3,1),(2,2), all
polygon-valid, with gap 574. These distinctions are explicit in the Lean
statements; no enlarged-family or auxiliary-direction failure is called a
root refutation.

An additional exact experiment marks these same 2/7 layers with z=1/100.
After multiplying every coefficient by the common denominator 10000, the
triple is [10311,325,14], with gap -38729. Algebraically the marked polynomial
is 1+3z(1+y)+z^2(11+25y+14y^2), and its adjacent gap is
z^2(-5+108z+471z^2). Thus coefficient LC for every positive degree marker
is too strong. degree-weight.json records this as an exact auxiliary
experiment, not an additional Lean theorem or a raw-source counterexample.

The A update also has the W/H minor x(z(1+y)-1). Its negative monomial
coefficient prevents a direct appeal to coefficientwise total positivity of
this displayed transfer matrix. This algebraic observation does not exclude
a different ordering, transformation, or more restricted source invariant.

Conjecture63 remains unresolved. No novelty claim. Formal acceptance status
is in evidence/markov-6a40862b/validation.json, not inferred from this text.

Use the inherited exact Pell summand

    H_s(q)=choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q).

Its center support for s>=2 is the integer interval
max(0,j-2s)<=q<=min(j,a-s). Fix q+r=k. On common center support put

    A(q)=(2s-j+q)(2s-1-j+q)/((a-s-q+1)(s+q-1)),
    B(q)=(a-s-q)(s+q)/((2s+2-j+q)(2s+1-j+q)),
    K=(s-1)(2s+1)/(s(2s-1)).

Elementary binomial ratios give the proposed identification

    [2 H_s(q)H_s(r)-H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(r)
                         -H_(s+1)(q)H_(s-1)(r)]/[H_s(q)H_s(r)]
      = 2-K[A(q)B(r)+A(r)B(q)].

The separate ratios are H_(s-1)(q)/H_s(q)=(s-1)/(2(2s-1))*A(q)
and H_(s+1)(q)/H_s(q)=2(2s+1)/s*B(q). The factors 0 and 1 in
the numerator preserve lower-strip zero cases, and a-s-q=0 preserves the
upper-strip endpoint. No coefficient normalization is proposed for the root:
division here is only for analyzing signed auxiliary layers with positive M.

    D(q,r)=AD(q) BD(q) AD(r) BD(r).

layerD6 record the literal numerators and denominators without cancellation.

    x=q+(j-r)/2, d=r-q-2, e=2s-j+q, h=a-s-r.

These four slacks are nonnegative. Translation by (j-r)/2 leaves all four
linear-factor pairs invariant. In reduced coordinates r=x+d+2,
s=(d+e+2)/2, j=r, a=s+r+h, exact expansion gives

theorem choose_upper_lc6 (n k : ℕ) :
    (n.choose k : ℤ)*(n+2).choose k ≤ ((n+1).choose k : ℤ)^2 := by
  by_cases hk : n<k
  · rw [Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt hk,Int.natCast_zero,zero_mul]
    exact sq_nonneg _
  · have hkn : k≤n := by omega
    have h1 : (n.choose k : ℤ)*(n+1)=((n+1).choose k : ℤ)*(n+1-k) := by
      have h := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => (x:ℤ)) (Nat.choose_mul_succ_eq n k)
      simpa only [Nat.cast_mul,Nat.cast_sub (show k≤n+1 by omega),
        Nat.cast_add,Nat.cast_one] using h
    have h2 : ((n+1).choose k : ℤ)*(n+2)=((n+2).choose k : ℤ)*(n+2-k) := by
      have h := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => (x:ℤ)) (Nat.choose_mul_succ_eq (n+1) k)
      have he : n+1+1=n+2 := by omega
      rw [he] at h
      simpa only [Nat.cast_mul,Nat.cast_sub (show k≤n+2 by omega),
        Nat.cast_add,Nat.cast_one,Nat.cast_ofNat] using h
    have hn : (0:ℤ)<n+1 := by omega
    have hm : (0:ℤ)<n+2-k := by omega
    have hid : ((n+1:ℤ)*(n+2-k))*
        (((n+1).choose k : ℤ)^2-(n.choose k : ℤ)*(n+2).choose k)=
        (k:ℤ)*((n+1).choose k : ℤ)^2 := by
      linear_combination -((n+2).choose k : ℤ)*(n+2-k)*h1 +
        ((n+1).choose k : ℤ)*(n+1-k)*h2
    have hprod : 0≤((n+1:ℤ)*(n+2-k))*
        (((n+1).choose k : ℤ)^2-(n.choose k : ℤ)*(n+2).choose k) := by
      rw [hid]; positivity
    have := (mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_left (mul_pos hn hm)).mp hprod
    linarith

theorem lc_product6 (a b c x y z : ℤ)
    (ha : 0≤a) (hc : 0≤c) (hy : 0≤y)
    (hab : a*c≤b^2) (hxy : x*z≤y^2) :

Machine-authored live request 9c20fccd3a9f4f1c9c9c9f443ef6f04b.

claim. Current-source compilation and kernel-replay receipts are authoritative

## Universal aggregation result

The inherited degree layer G_w(s,d;y) sums exactly those s-cut mask weights
whose individual degree is d. Multiplicity is retained. The new theorem
single_degree_layer_lc9c20 proves ordinary coefficient log-concavity of
G_w(1,d;y) for every finite Boolean word w, every natural degree d, and every
natural starting index k. There is no word-length or denominator bound.
The integer version single_degree_layer_integer_lc9c20 and exact marked-source
specialization are in MarkovSingleLayerInteger9c20; consult validation.json
for final status. Zero layers and coefficients beyond the degree are included.

The proof is an aggregation argument, not an inference from individual-term LC.
Write

    R_n(y)=1+2y+...+2y^n,
    P_n(y)=R_n(y)+y^(n+1).

A mask with one selected cut has weight equal to its preceding gap weight,
times either 1 or 1+y according to the selected letter. Skipped letters
after that cut contribute one. The checked gap classification says the
preceding gap weight is some R_n or P_n. Exact degree computation therefore
restricts every degree-d one-cut term, for d>=2, to four shapes:

    R_d, P_(d-1), (1+y)R_(d-1), (1+y)P_(d-2).

For arbitrary nonnegative real a,b,c,e the mixture of these shapes is LC.
For d>=3 its coefficient list is

    a+b+c+e,
    2a+2b+3c+3e,
    2a+2b+4c+4e  (at indices 2 through d-2),
    2a+2b+4c+3e,
    2a+b+2c+e.

The middle range may be empty. The first and final nontrivial gaps are
nonnegative polynomial expressions in a,b,c,e; the middle plateau and
transition inequalities are checked as well. Degree two is the separate
quadratic with coefficients [a+b+c+e,2a+2b+3c+2e,2a+b+2c+e].
For d<2 every product of coefficients two positions apart has a zero factor.
The proof uses no coefficient division and no root-location assumption.

singleMaskSum_shape9c20 supplies the missing combinatorial bridge: the sum
of ANY finite list of one-cut masks of one degree has the displayed mixture
form with nonnegative parameters. Applying it to the exact filtered mask list
gives the theorem. Integer-to-real transport is by a proved polynomial ring map,
not a normalization. degreeCoeff_layer07a7 identifies the same layer by ordinary
coefficient extraction in the auxiliary degree marker.

This result does not justify summing different degrees. It also does not
establish any complete pinned direction for arbitrary sources. The first and
second complete lower diagonals already have separate inherited source proofs;
the present result addresses a proposed aggregation mechanism for higher slices.

import MathGKM.MarkovLogConcavity

namespace MathGKM.Markov
noncomputable section
open Polynomial

def edgeEval : BiPoly →+* ℝ[X] :=
  (Polynomial.mapRingHom (Int.castRingHom ℝ)).comp
    (Polynomial.mapRingHom (Polynomial.evalRingHom (0 : ℤ)))

@[simp] theorem edgeEval_U : edgeEval U = X := by simp [edgeEval, U]
@[simp] theorem edgeEval_V : edgeEval V = 0 := by simp [edgeEval, V]
@[simp] theorem edgeEval_S : edgeEval S = X+1 := by simp [S]

def EdgeFormula (l : Label) : Prop :=
  0 < l.b ∧ edgeEval l.p = X^l.a * (X+1)^(l.b-1)

def FrameEdge (f : Frame) : Prop :=
  EdgeFormula f.lo ∧ EdgeFormula f.mid ∧ EdgeFormula f.hi

theorem edge_initial : FrameEdge initial := by
  constructor
  · norm_num [EdgeFormula, initial]
  constructor
  · simp [EdgeFormula, initial]
    ring
  · simp [EdgeFormula, initial]

theorem edge_step (x y z : Label) (hx : EdgeFormula x) (hy : EdgeFormula y) :
    EdgeFormula ⟨x.a+y.a,x.b+y.b,S*x.p*y.p-U^x.a*V^x.b*z.p⟩ := by
  obtain ⟨hxb,hxp⟩ := hx
  obtain ⟨hyb,hyp⟩ := hy
  constructor
  · dsimp; omega
  · dsimp
    simp only [map_sub, map_mul, map_pow, edgeEval_S, edgeEval_U, edgeEval_V]
    rw [zero_pow (by omega : x.b ≠ 0), mul_zero, zero_mul, sub_zero, hxp, hyp]
    have hexp : x.b+y.b-1 = (x.b-1)+(y.b-1)+1 := by omega
    rw [hexp, pow_add, pow_add, pow_one, pow_add]
    ring

theorem edge_advance {f : Frame} (h : FrameEdge f) (right : Bool) :
    FrameEdge (advance f right) := by
  obtain ⟨hl,hm,hr⟩ := h
  cases right
  · exact ⟨hl, edge_step f.lo f.mid f.hi hl hm, hm⟩
  · refine ⟨hm, ?_, hr⟩
    have hh := edge_step f.hi f.mid f.lo hr hm
    simpa [advance, Nat.add_comm] using hh

theorem edge_fold (path : List Bool) (f : Frame) (h : FrameEdge f) :
    FrameEdge (path.foldl advance f) := by
  induction path generalizing f with
  | nil => exact h
  | cons b bs ih => exact ih (advance f b) (edge_advance h b)

/-- All finite paths, with no denominator bound. -/
theorem boundary_formula (path : List Bool) :
    edgeEval (frame path).mid.p =
      X^(frame path).mid.a * (X+1)^((frame path).mid.b-1) :=
  (edge_fold path initial edge_initial).2.1.2

theorem coeffSeq_X_mul (p : ℝ[X]) :
    CoeffSeq (X*p) = fun k => CoeffSeq p (k-1) := by
  funext k
  by_cases hk : k < 0
  · simp [CoeffSeq, hk, show k-1 < 0 by omega]
  · lift k to ℕ using (show 0 ≤ k by omega)
    cases k with
    | zero => simp [CoeffSeq]
    | succ n =>
      simp [CoeffSeq, show ¬ (↑n+1 : ℤ) < 0 by omega,
        show ¬ (↑n : ℤ) < 0 by omega]

theorem crossLC_X_mul {p : ℝ[X]} (h : CrossLC (CoeffSeq p)) :
    CrossLC (CoeffSeq (X*p)) := by
  rw [coeffSeq_X_mul]
  exact crossLC_shift h (-1)

theorem crossLC_binomial (n : ℕ) : CrossLC (CoeffSeq ((1+X)^n)) := by
  have h := crossLC_pascal (crossLC_quad (A:=1) (B:=0) (C:=0)
    (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)) n
  rw [← coeffSeq_quadratic, ← coeffSeq_binomial_mul] at h
  simpa [Quadratic] using h

theorem crossLC_X_pow_binomial (a n : ℕ) :
    CrossLC (CoeffSeq (X^a*(1+X)^n)) := by
  induction a with
  | zero => simpa using crossLC_binomial n
  | succ a ih => simpa [pow_succ', mul_assoc] using crossLC_X_mul ih

/-- Universal log-concavity of the j=0 boundary of every generated numerator. -/
theorem boundary_logConcave (path : List Bool) (k : ℤ) :
    let f := CoeffSeq (edgeEval (frame path).mid.p)
    f (k-1)*f (k+1) ≤ f k^2 := by
  dsimp only
  rw [boundary_formula]
  simpa [add_comm] using crossLC_adjacent
    (crossLC_X_pow_binomial (frame path).mid.a ((frame path).mid.b-1)) k

theorem edgeEval_coeff (P : BiPoly) (i : ℕ) :
    (edgeEval P).coeff i = (coeff P i 0 : ℝ) := by
  simp [edgeEval, coeff, ← Polynomial.coeff_zero_eq_eval_zero]

/-- The same universal result, stated literally in the target's raw coefficients. -/
theorem boundary_raw_logConcave (path : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    coeff (frame path).mid.p i 0 * coeff (frame path).mid.p (i+2) 0 ≤
      coeff (frame path).mid.p (i+1) 0 ^ 2 := by
  have h := boundary_logConcave path (↑i+1)
  dsimp only at h
  have hn : ¬ (↑i : ℤ) < 0 := by omega
  have hn1 : ¬ (↑i+1 : ℤ) < 0 := by omega
  have hn2 : ¬ (↑i+1+1 : ℤ) < 0 := by omega
  simp only [CoeffSeq, add_sub_cancel_right, hn, hn1, hn2, if_false,
    Int.toNat_natCast, edgeEval_coeff] at h
  exact_mod_cast h

end
